basis: Progressive intracranial arterial stenosis; ischemic brain injury is common, with intellectual disability and seizures reported in 30-79%.
Germ cell malignancy arising in the central nervous system.
Umbrella for defective peroxisomal oxidation; additional organ damage is not shared consistently across its subtypes.
Localized cutaneous mucin accumulation produces persistent papules without systemic involvement.
Cholesterol-associated lipoid pneumonia affects lung tissue; local cholesterol accumulation does not establish a systemic lipid disorder.
Cutaneous mast-cell proliferation causes generalized skin infiltration and blistering; cardiorespiratory arrest occurs in only 5-29%.
Calcium-sensing disorder; osteomalacia is annotated in 30-79%. Altered renal calcium handling alone is not kidney injury; pulmonary ancestry conflicts with the definition.
Congenital craniofacial fusion defect classified as a facial skeletal disorder; oral, nasal and eyelid involvement varies across subtypes.
Autoimmune skin fibrosis and microvasculopathy define CREST; esophageal dysfunction is a cardinal feature, affecting roughly 50-90%. These four axes fill the cap.
Estrogen synthesis deficiency; osteopenia/osteoporosis occurs in 80-99%. Hepatic steatosis is a separately diagnosed metabolic liver complication.
Epilepsy syndrome involving generalized and focal seizures.
Inherited pulmonary cystic disease with pneumothorax; recurrent infections alone do not establish an immune deficiency.
Glycosylation disorder with defining skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic injury; soft skin alone is insufficient.
Malignancy-associated calcium imbalance; acute neurologic and cardiovascular symptoms do not establish common lasting organ injury or a blood-cell disorder.
Acute myeloid leukemia defined by a cytogenetic rearrangement; primary disease of marrow and myeloid blood cells.
Congenital duplication of rectal tissue; urinary infections and perianal sepsis are secondary complications rather than defining organ involvement.
Anterior spinal arterial ischemia defines a vascular spinal cord injury with motor and sensory loss.
Mast-cell activation is a leukocyte and immune-mediated disorder; episodic mediator symptoms do not establish lasting injury in additional organs.
Renal phosphate-wasting disorder causes hypophosphatemia; intracerebral calcification is specified, but associated functional brain injury is not established.
Primary abnormal reduction of intraocular pressure.
Microcephaly and severe limb reduction define the syndrome. Pulmonary hypoplasia and other malformations are reported, but their frequencies are unspecified.
Peripheral axonal neuropathy and congenital scalp aplasia define the syndrome; associated calvarial bone defects occurred in 3/3 reported patients.
Carcinoma originating in the intrahepatic bile ducts.
Congenital digit malformation with metacarpal and metatarsal fusion; associated skin webbing is part of the limb malformation.
Infectious or immune-mediated inflammation of the retina and optic nerve; the optic nerve belongs to the ocular axis.
